html:
The Deni are an Indigenous people of the western Amazon in Brazil, living along tributaries of the Purus and Juruá rivers in Amazonas state. They speak a language of the small Arawan family.

They live in villages along the rivers, fishing, hunting and farming manioc in forest gardens. Like their neighbours, they lost people and land during the rubber boom of the late 1800s and early 1900s. In the early 2000s, after years of pressure, their land was officially marked out as an Indigenous territory, which protects it from loggers. See also the wider Amazon peoples.
